truth: a BWebServlet that writes and verifies no CSRF token (no verifyCsrfToken( call, no CsrfProtectedFilter,
and no X-Requested-With guard, which lint-servlet csrf-xrw-only owns) WARNs once, at the class line; a
token only in a comment (A.java), or a local merely named csrfToken (C.java), is no check. B.java has the
X-Requested-With guard: lint-servlet reports it.
-- args --
@DIR@/m
-- want --
exit 0
WARN  no-csrf  @DIR@/m/A.java:2  servlet writes but verifies no CSRF token: call CsrfUtil.verifyCsrfToken(op.getRequest()) before the write, or map CsrfProtectedFilter on its write verbs (types/servlet-write.md)
WARN  no-csrf  @DIR@/m/C.java:1  servlet writes but verifies no CSRF token: call CsrfUtil.verifyCsrfToken(op.getRequest()) before the write, or map CsrfProtectedFilter on its write verbs (types/servlet-write.md)
-- stderr --
-- m/A.java --
// csrfToken in a comment is no check
public class A extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
    target.set(p, v, op);
  }
}
-- m/B.java --
public class B extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    if (!"XMLHttpRequest".equals(op.getRequest().getHeader("X-Requested-With"))) return;
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
    target.set(p, v, op);
  }
}
-- m/C.java --
public class C extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    String csrfToken = "unused";
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
    target.set(p, v, op);
  }
}
